close_reason: Replaced m.len()-based counter with a per-(type, account) monotonic counter in Inner.next_ids (feature-gated to non-realistic-demo-ids mode). Counter increments on every mint and never decrements on delete, so a destroyed id is never re-minted. 3 new unit tests lock in the fix. Calendars-server and chat-server have the same shape; workspace sweep tracked at bd:JMAP-h7jp (note: the commit message in 0d14538 incorrectly references JMAP-yfax — the actual workspace sweep bead is JMAP-h7jp). Implementation in commit 0d14538.
description:
Trigger (only without the realistic-demo-ids feature, i.e. the default deterministic mode):

  let b = MemoryBackend::new().with_account('a');
  let (id1, _) = b.create_object(&(), &Id::from('a'), 'c1', book1).await?;  // id = 'addressbook0000000000000001'
  b.destroy_object::<AddressBook>(&(), &Id::from('a'), &id1).await?;        // store now empty (len=0)
  let (id2, _) = b.create_object(&(), &Id::from('a'), 'c2', book2).await?;  // re-mints 'addressbook0000000000000001'!

memory.rs:314 computes n = inner.objects_ref(...).map_or(0, |m| m.len()) and then formats new_id from n+1. After a delete, len() goes down, and the next create re-mints the same id as the one that was just destroyed.

For the change_log this is a real problem: the same Id now appears in destroyed (entry K) AND in created (entry K+2), and a /changes call spanning before K to after K+2 returns destroyed: [id1] AND created: [id1] for the same logical Id. RFC 8620 §5.2 says state strings 'MUST be different in different cases' — this re-mints, which violates the spirit. The de-dup logic at memory.rs:438-456 silently makes the re-minted id appear ONLY in destroyed because the loop sees destroyed second; that's another silent-correctness issue.

The debug_assert at memory.rs:318-325 is the saving grace IN DEBUG BUILDS — it fires if the new_id already exists in the map. But it only fires when the SAME id is still in the map. After a destroy the id is GONE from the map, so the debug_assert does NOT fire. The collision is silent in both debug and release.

The big block comment at lines 308-313 explicitly says 'collides after deletes (count goes down, next id re-uses)'. So the implementor knows. But knowing-and-shipping is not the same as fixing. Two options:

 (a) Switch the default to the timestamp+atomic counter (the realistic-demo-ids feature) and delete the deterministic mode entirely. The comment already says both modes are demonstration-quality and persistent backends need ULIDs.
 (b) Use a monotonic counter that doesn't reset on delete — store next_id in Inner and increment it forever, mod nothing.

Option (b) is the minimal fix and preserves the 'lex-orderable within a (type, account)' property the deterministic mode is documented to have. Option (a) is the bigger cleanup.

Note: this is a sibling-pattern issue, not unique to contacts. Calendars-server and chat-server have the same demo_next_id shape (verified via grep). If the fix lands here it should propagate to those siblings per the canonical-template rule.
title: demo_next_id len()-based deterministic mode collides after a delete; debug_assert fires on round-trip create/destroy/create
